text: Most leaders, especially technical leaders, assume they have to have all the answers. People have climbed the ladder because they've been dependable, reliable, the smartest person in the room.
speaker: Rachel Lockett
context: Lenny asks Rachel about the biggest gap that keeps leaders from being successful. Rachel explains that many technical leaders believe they must have all the answers because they've advanced in their careers by being the smartest person in the room. However, this approach backfires at scale - constantly providing solutions doesn't develop team capability, it creates dependency where everyone brings problems to the leader instead of solving them independently.
text_ko: 대부분의 리더들, 특히 기술 리더들(technical leaders)은 모든 답을 알아야 한다고 생각해요. 사람들은 믿음직하고 신뢰할 수 있었고 회의실에서 가장 똑똑한 사람이었기 때문에 승진해 왔어요.
text_zh: 大多数领导，尤其是技术领导(technical leaders)，常常以为自己得知道所有答案。很多人能爬上来，是因为他们一直很靠谱、让人放心，而且通常是团队里最聪明的那个人。
text_es: La mayoría de los líderes, sobre todo los técnicos, asumen que deben tener todas las respuestas. Muchos han ascendido porque han sido de fiar, constantes y los más preparados de la sala.
key_sentence: Most leaders, especially technical leaders, assume they have to have all the answers.
original_text: Most leaders, especially technical leaders, assume they have to have all the answers. People have climbed the ladder because they've been dependable, reliable, the smartest person in the room. But great leaders know that when you try to advise and have the answer all the time, you're not actually equipping your team to go solve the hard problems. You're training your team to come to you with all of the hard problems.

vocabulary.definition: To take for granted or without proof; to suppose something to be true based on a belief or expectation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, leaders often assume they possess all the necessary knowledge or solutions, which can lead to overconfidence and hinder collaboration.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'assume' can imply a reasonable expectation, it may also carry a negative connotation of negligence or lack of inquiry.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of being relied on; trustworthy and consistent in performance or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, being dependable is crucial for team dynamics, as it fosters trust and ensures that tasks are completed reliably.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of stability and consistency, making it particularly valuable in roles that require accountability.

vocabulary.definition: Consistently good in quality or performance; able to be trusted to perform well.
vocabulary.businessContext: Reliability is a key attribute for products and services in business, as it directly impacts customer satisfaction and brand loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: While similar to 'dependable', 'reliable' often emphasizes the quality and consistency of performance over time.

text: People, when they want to have a conflict, they come in ready to prove their point. There's a misguided view that the goal is to convince the other person that what they're doing is wrong.
speaker: Rachel Lockett
context: Lenny asks Rachel how to make difficult conversations less difficult. Rachel explains that most people approach conflict with the wrong mindset - they enter conversations armored and focused on proving their point or convincing others they're wrong. She argues this is fundamentally misguided because productive conflict should aim for mutual understanding rather than winning or being right.
text_ko: 사람들은 갈등을 하려고 하면 이미 자기 주장을 증명하려고 들어와요. 상대방을 설득해서 '네가 틀렸다'고 만드는 게 목표라고 보는 건 오해예요.
text_zh: 人们一有分歧，往往就准备好要证明自己的观点是对的。一个错误的观念是，以为目标是把对方说服过来，让他们承认自己错了。
text_es: La gente, cuando busca un conflicto, va preparada para demostrar que tiene razón. Hay una idea equivocada de que el objetivo es convencer al otro de que lo que hace está mal.
key_sentence: There's a misguided view that the goal is to convince the other person that what they're doing is wrong.
original_text: People, when they want to have a conflict, they come in ready to prove their point. There's a misguided view that the goal is to convince the other person that what they're doing is wrong. Actually, the goal of any conflict is to create mutual understanding.

vocabulary.definition: Based on faulty reasoning or understanding; leading to incorrect conclusions or actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a misguided strategy may result from poor market analysis or misunderstanding customer needs, leading to ineffective decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'misguided' often implies a lack of judgment, it can also suggest a well-intentioned but ultimately flawed approach.

vocabulary.definition: To persuade someone to believe or do something through reasoning or argument.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales and marketing, the ability to convince potential clients of a product's value is crucial for closing deals and driving revenue.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'convince' suggests a strong persuasive effort, it can sometimes carry a negative connotation if perceived as manipulative.

text: When people are in their gifts and their strengths, they have more energy. We all have more energy when we're operating from the things we naturally are good at. It's no one else's job to help you live in your gifts.
speaker: Rachel Lockett
context: Lenny asks about Rachel's advice for helping leaders avoid burnout. Rachel shares her core philosophy that people have more energy when operating in their natural strengths and gifts. She emphasizes personal accountability, pointing out that employees often wrongly expect managers to make their jobs more engaging, when actually it's each person's responsibility to align their career with their strengths over time.
text_ko: 사람들이 자신의 강점에서 일할 때 에너지가 훨씬 많아요. 우리 모두 본래 잘하는 일을 할 때 더 힘이 나고요. 자신의 강점을 살려 사는 건 다른 사람이 해줘야 할 일이 아니에요.
text_zh: 当你把天赋和优势用上的时候，会更有能量。做自己天生擅长的事，会更有干劲。别指望别人来替你发挥天赋，这事得靠你自己。
text_es: Cuando las personas están en su elemento, usando sus talentos y fortalezas, tienen más energía. Todos tenemos más energía cuando trabajamos desde aquello en lo que naturalmente somos buenos. Nadie tiene la obligación de ayudarte a vivir desde tus talentos.
key_sentence: Operate in your gifts to have more energy and navigate your career.
original_text: When people are in their gifts and their strengths, they have more energy. We all have more energy when we're operating from the things we naturally are good at. It's no one else's job to help you live in your gifts. What I notice in big companies is people are often annoyed or frustrated with their management for not making their job more interesting. No, your manager's job is to help you perform in the job you are hired to do. It's your job to navigate your career.

vocabulary.definition: Functioning or performing actions based on a specific set of values, principles, or strengths.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'operating from' often refers to making decisions that align with an organization's core values or an individual's strengths.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a proactive approach to leveraging one's capabilities, and is best used in discussions about strategic alignment or personal effectiveness.

text: I think that most leaders, especially technical leaders, assume they have to have all the answers. People have climbed the ladder in whatever realm they're in because they've been dependable, reliable, the smartest person in the room.
speaker: Rachel Lockett
context: Rachel elaborates on why the traditional approach of having all the answers fails at scale. She explains that while technical leaders advanced by being reliable and knowledgeable, at rapidly growing companies they actually have less context than their team members. The old approach becomes impossible because leaders can't deeply understand every problem when the company scales.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 대부분의 리더들, 특히 기술 리더(technical leaders)들은 모든 답을 다 알고 있어야 한다고 생각하는 경우가 많아요. 사람들이 자기 분야에서 승진해 온 건 믿음직하고 신뢰할 만했고, 그 방에서 가장 똑똑한 사람이었기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得大多数领导，尤其是技术型领导，常常以为自己必须有所有答案。他们能在各自领域往上爬，往往是因为一直很靠谱、让人放心，而且通常是圈子里最聪明的那个人。
text_es: La mayoría de los líderes, sobre todo los técnicos, creen que deben tener todas las respuestas. Muchas personas han ascendido en su carrera porque se les considera fiables, responsables y los más inteligentes de la sala.
key_sentence: most leaders, especially technical leaders, assume they have to have all the answers.
original_text: I think that most leaders, especially technical leaders, assume they have to have all the answers. People have climbed the ladder in whatever realm they're in because they've been dependable, reliable, the smartest person in the room. But when you're leading a quickly-scaling company, you quickly have less context than the people you're around. And the way you were operating before doesn't work because you don't have the ability to wrap your arms around every problem in a deep way.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of being relied on; trustworthy and consistent in performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being dependable is crucial for building strong relationships with clients and colleagues, as it fosters trust and ensures that commitments are met.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used positively, over-reliance on a single dependable individual can lead to bottlenecks in decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Consistently good in quality or performance; able to be trusted to perform well.
vocabulary.businessContext: Reliability is a key attribute for products and services in the tech industry, as it directly impacts customer satisfaction and brand reputation.
vocabulary.nuance: Although similar to 'dependable,' 'reliable' often emphasizes the quality of output rather than the character of the individual.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who possess advanced knowledge and expertise in a specific technical field and guide teams or organizations in that domain.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech companies, technical leaders are often responsible for driving innovation, mentoring team members, and making critical decisions on technology implementation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies not only technical proficiency but also the ability to lead and influence others, which can sometimes create pressure to always have the right answers.

text: What I notice in big companies is people are often annoyed or frustrated with their management for not making their job more interesting. No, your manager's job is to help you perform in the job you are hired to do.
speaker: Rachel Lockett
context: In discussing burnout prevention, Rachel addresses a common misconception she observes in large companies. Many employees expect their managers to make their roles more engaging or interesting, but Rachel clarifies that managers are responsible for helping people succeed in their current role, while career navigation and finding fulfilling work is each individual's personal responsibility.
text_ko: 큰 회사에서 자주 보는 건 사람들이 경영진(management)이 자기 일을 더 흥미롭게 만들어주지 않는다고 짜증 내거나 답답해한다는 거예요. 아니에요. 매니저(manager)의 역할은 당신이 채용된 그 일을 잘 해낼 수 있도록 도와주는 거예요.
text_zh: 我在大公司常看到，很多人因为管理层没让工作更有意思而对经理不满。其实不是这样的：经理的工作是帮你把被雇来做的那份本职工作做好。
text_es: En las grandes empresas veo que mucha gente se frustra con la dirección (management) porque espera que haga su trabajo más interesante. No: el trabajo de tu jefe (manager) es ayudarte a rendir en el puesto para el que te contrataron.
key_sentence: It's your job to navigate your career, not your manager's.
original_text: What I notice in big companies is people are often annoyed or frustrated with their management for not making their job more interesting. No, your manager's job is to help you perform in the job you are hired to do. It's your job to navigate your career.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling upset or annoyed as a result of being unable to change or achieve something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, employees may feel frustrated when they encounter obstacles that hinder their productivity or when management fails to provide adequate support.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'frustrated' conveys a sense of dissatisfaction, it can also imply a desire for improvement or change in the situation.

vocabulary.definition: To carry out a task or function, especially in a professional context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, employees are expected to perform their roles effectively to meet organizational goals and contribute to overall success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'perform' often emphasizes the execution of specific duties and can imply a standard of quality or effectiveness.

text: So I try to help my leaders see that they can design their lives so they're spending 80% of their time in their gifts. That seems really ambitious because you're stuck within a context that requires a lot of you.
speaker: Rachel Lockett
context: Rachel discusses helping leaders avoid burnout by operating in their strengths most of the time. She acknowledges this 80% goal seems ambitious given organizational constraints, especially for executives at large companies. She notes that founders face a particular challenge because their roles evolve dramatically as companies scale, often moving them away from the work that originally inspired them to start the business.
text_ko: 저는 리더들이 자신의 삶을 설계해서 시간의 80%를 자신의 강점에 쓸 수 있다는 걸 보게 도와주려고 해요. 그런데 그건 정말 야심차게 들려요. 지금 처한 맥락이 워낙 많은 걸 요구하니까요.
text_zh: 我尽量让我的领导们看到，他们其实可以把生活设计成把80%的时间花在自己最擅长、最有价值的事情上。但这听起来很有野心，因为你常常被现有的环境束缚，要承担很多职能和责任，精力被分散了。
text_es: Por eso procuro ayudar a los líderes con los que trabajo a ver que pueden diseñar sus vidas para dedicar el 80% de su tiempo a lo que mejor saben hacer. Eso suena muy ambicioso, porque están inmersos en un contexto que les exige muchísimo.
key_sentence: Leaders can design their lives to spend 80% of their time in their gifts.
original_text: So I try to help my leaders see that they can design their lives so they're spending 80% of their time in their gifts. That seems really ambitious because you're stuck within a context that requires a lot of you. Especially when you're executive at a huge company. But I also interact with founders who started a company with great inspiration, an entrepreneurial vision, and their job has obviously changed every six months.

vocabulary.definition: Having a strong desire and determination to achieve success or a specific goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being ambitious often refers to setting high targets for growth, innovation, or market expansion, and striving to exceed them.
vocabulary.nuance: While ambition is generally viewed positively, it can imply a relentless pursuit that may overlook collaboration or ethical considerations.

vocabulary.definition: The circumstances or setting in which an event occurs, which can influence its meaning and interpretation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, understanding the context is crucial for making informed decisions and crafting strategies that are relevant to the specific market or organizational environment.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply that certain factors must be considered to fully grasp a situation, emphasizing the importance of situational awareness.
